stem: In her school science class in Pune, Meera observes an Amoeba (a single cell) under the microscope, while her classmate Arjun sketches a neem plant (made of many cells). Which of the following statements about how living organisms are built from cells is correct: () A. Only large organisms like the neem plant are made of cells, while tiny organisms like Amoeba are not made of cells; B. All living organisms are made of cells, whether they have one cell like Amoeba or many cells like the neem plant; C. Only organisms with many cells can carry out life processes, so a single cell cannot be a complete organism; D. Cells are found only in plants and animals, and not in microorganisms

options.text: Only large organisms like the neem plant are made of cells, while tiny organisms like Amoeba are not made of cells
All living organisms are made of cells, whether they have one cell like Amoeba or many cells like the neem plant
Only organisms with many cells can carry out life processes, so a single cell cannot be a complete organism
Cells are found only in plants and animals, and not in microorganisms

teacher.key_rationale: The cell is the basic unit of life: a unicellular organism (Amoeba) is a single complete cell, and a multicellular organism (neem plant) is built from many cells. Options A and D wrongly exclude microorganisms from being cell-based; option C wrongly denies that one cell can be a complete organism.
